neighborhoods.name: Ballantyne
neighborhoods.tagline: A planned south Charlotte district of offices, retail, golf, and newer neighborhoods
overview: Ballantyne is a roughly 2,000-acre planned district at Charlotte's southern edge, next to the South Carolina state line. It grew up around the Ballantyne Corporate Park and the Ballantyne Hotel starting in the 1990s, and it now mixes office campuses, apartments, townhome communities, and established single-family subdivisions. Recent redevelopment has added a public park and amphitheater area at the former corporate campus core.

For buyers, Ballantyne usually means newer construction by Charlotte standards, homeowners' associations, and quick access to I-485 and Johnston Road (US 521). Ballantyne Country Club offers a private golf community, while other subdivisions range from townhomes to larger custom homes. Daily errands are handled by several nearby shopping centers, and the Four Mile Creek Greenway offers a paved trail through the area. Ballantyne addresses use ZIP code 28277, which also covers neighboring communities, so buyers should confirm the exact subdivision when comparing listings.
shopping: Shopping centers along Ballantyne Commons Pkwy and Johnston Rd

faq.q: What ZIP code is Ballantyne in?
faq.a: Ballantyne is in ZIP code 28277.

faq.q: Is Ballantyne near the light rail?
faq.a: No. Ballantyne is not on a LYNX rail line; most residents commute by car via I-485 and Johnston Road (US 521).

faq.q: Is there golf in Ballantyne?
faq.a: Yes. Ballantyne Country Club is a private golf community within the area.

Housing here is mostly single-family subdivisions built from the 1990s onward, with a scattering of townhome communities. Most neighborhoods have homeowners' associations, and many include pools or clubhouses. Residents are a short drive from Ballantyne's office and shopping core, the Blakeney and Stonecrest-area retail centers on Rea Road, and I-485. Because this is a portal-defined name rather than a recorded subdivision, buyers should look at the specific subdivision and HOA for each home they are considering. Commuters typically use I-485 to reach the airport or Uptown, and Johnston Road for local trips.

Buyers should rely on the recorded subdivision name and the property's municipal jurisdiction (City of Charlotte vs. Town of Pineville), which affects taxes and services. neighborhoods.name: Barclay Downs
neighborhoods.tagline: Established mid-century streets on the doorstep of SouthPark Mall
overview: Barclay Downs is an established residential neighborhood on the west side of SouthPark, close enough to SouthPark Mall that many residents can reach the shops on foot. Its curving streets were developed largely in the mid-20th century, and the neighborhood has a mature tree canopy.

The original housing stock is mostly ranch and split-level homes, and over the years many lots have seen renovations or new custom homes. Being in the SouthPark area puts residents near the mall, Phillips Place, office towers along Fairview and Morrison, and Symphony Park, the outdoor venue next to the mall. Commutes typically use Fairview Road, Sharon Road, and Park Road. Barclay Downs spans parts of the 28209 and 28211 ZIP codes. Because the neighborhood is so close to SouthPark's commercial core, buyers often weigh walkability to shops against the traffic that comes with a busy retail district.

neighborhoods.name: Belmont (Charlotte)
neighborhoods.tagline: Historic in-town Charlotte neighborhood near NoDa—not the City of Belmont
overview: Belmont is a historic neighborhood just northeast of Uptown Charlotte, between Villa Heights and the Plaza Midwood area. It should not be confused with the separate City of Belmont in Gaston County, roughly 12 miles west. Belmont developed in the early 20th century, and its grid of small lots still reflects that era.

Housing is a mix of early-1900s cottages and bungalows, many renovated, and newer infill homes and townhomes that have been built on vacant or redeveloped lots. The neighborhood is close to Optimist Hall, the Parkwood LYNX Blue Line station, and the restaurants of Plaza Midwood and NoDa. Uptown is a short drive or bike ride away. Most addresses fall in ZIP code 28205, with some in 28206. Buyers should expect a mix of renovated originals and new construction on the same block, which can widen the range of prices and lot sizes.
dining: Plaza Midwood and NoDa restaurant districts (nearby)

faq.q: Is Belmont in Charlotte the same as the City of Belmont?
faq.a: No. This Belmont is a neighborhood in Charlotte (ZIP 28205/28206). The City of Belmont is a separate municipality in Gaston County.

faq.q: What ZIP code is the Belmont neighborhood in?
faq.a: Mostly 28205, with some addresses in 28206.

faq.q: Is Belmont near the light rail?
faq.a: Yes. The LYNX Blue Line's Parkwood station is nearby.

overview: Beverly Woods is an established south Charlotte neighborhood located southwest of SouthPark near Park Road and Sharon Road. Developed largely in the 1960s and 1970s, it is known for large wooded lots, rolling streets, and a quiet residential character.

Homes are primarily brick ranches, split-levels, and two-story traditional houses, and many have been updated or expanded over the years. The location is central for south Charlotte: SouthPark's shopping and offices are a few minutes away, Park Road Park offers sports fields and a lake, and Quail Hollow's corridor is just south. The area is in ZIP code 28210. Beverly Woods is not on the light rail, and most residents travel by car on Park Road, Sharon Road, and Fairview Road. Many streets have no through traffic, and lot sizes are generally larger than in the older in-town neighborhoods closer to Uptown.

Its location puts residents a short walk or drive from Plaza Midwood's Central Avenue restaurants and shops, and Uptown is only a few miles away. Most addresses are in ZIP code 28205, with a portion in 28204. Its small size and limited through streets give Chantilly a tucked-away feel even though Independence Boulevard and Central Avenue are close. Buyers interested in renovation should check lot sizes and any setback rules before planning additions.

neighborhoods.tagline: A historic neighborhood next to Midtown and the Little Sugar Creek Greenway
overview: Cherry is one of Charlotte's oldest neighborhoods, located just southeast of Uptown near Midtown. It is a historically African-American neighborhood, developed in the late 1800s and early 1900s, and it is bounded by Little Sugar Creek, Kenilworth Avenue, the John Belk Freeway (I-277), East 4th Street, Queens Road, and Henley Place.

The housing stock combines older cottages and bungalows with a growing number of newer townhomes and single-family infill. Cherry sits beside the Little Sugar Creek Greenway and the Midtown shopping district, and Uptown is about a mile away. Its central location gives easy access to Kings Drive, Kenilworth Avenue, and I-277. Cherry is in ZIP code 28204. Cherry's proximity to Uptown has brought significant redevelopment pressure in recent years, so buyers may find older homes and brand-new townhomes on the same street. Kings Drive and the greenway also connect easily to Dilworth and Myers Park.

overview: Elizabeth is one of Charlotte's oldest in-town neighborhoods, just east of Uptown. It grew around an 1891 streetcar line and takes its name from Elizabeth College, a women's college once located where Novant Health Presbyterian Medical Center now stands. Central Piedmont Community College's central campus and American Legion Memorial Stadium are on the neighborhood's edges. Elizabeth is in ZIP code 28204. Hawthorne Lane and 7th Street link Elizabeth to Plaza Midwood and Chantilly, and the Little Sugar Creek Greenway runs along the neighborhood's southern side toward Midtown. Parking can be tight near the hospital and college.

overview: South End is a high-density commercial and residential district immediately southwest of Uptown. Once an industrial corridor along the rail line, it has been transformed since the LYNX Blue Line opened in 2007, and it now has towers of apartments and condos, offices, breweries, restaurants, and shops.

The Charlotte Rail Trail runs alongside the light rail through the heart of South End, connecting stations such as Carson, Bland Street, East/West Boulevard, and New Bern. South End is a Municipal Service District and is in ZIP code 28203. Many condo buildings include amenities such as fitness centers and rooftop spaces, and HOA fees vary widely, so buyers should compare dues and what they cover.

Phillips Place, an open-air shopping and dining center, sits across Fairview Road, and Symphony Park hosts outdoor concerts. Commutes rely on Fairview Road, Sharon Road, and Providence Road. SouthPark spans ZIP codes 28210 and 28211. The district has grown denser in recent decades with condominium towers, office buildings, and hotels. Buyers will find a wide range of options, from established single-family neighborhoods to condo buildings within walking distance of the mall.

overview: Fourth Ward is Uptown Charlotte's northwest quadrant and its most historic residential area. It features restored Victorian homes, Old Settlers' Cemetery, and Fourth Ward Park.

The neighborhood is known for its quiet, tree-lined streets, Fourth Ward Park, and Old Settlers' Cemetery, one of the oldest burial grounds in Charlotte. Residents can walk to Uptown offices, restaurants, the Blumenthal theaters, and Discovery Place Science. Buyers will find historic single-family homes, townhomes, and condos.

overview: South Charlotte is a broad, informal name for the southern part of the city, generally stretching from the SouthPark and Quail Hollow areas south to Ballantyne and the South Carolina line, and east toward Providence Road. It is not an official district, and different people draw its edges differently.

The area contains many of the neighborhoods in this guide, including SouthPark, Carmel, Quail Hollow, Piper Glen, Blakeney, Rea Farms, and Ballantyne. Housing ranges from 1960s ranches on wooded lots near SouthPark to golf communities and 2000s subdivisions closer to I-485. Major routes include Providence Road (NC 16), Carmel Road, Park Road, Johnston Road (US 521), Rea Road, NC 51, and I-485. South Charlotte is largely car-oriented; the LYNX Blue Line runs along its western edge on South Boulevard. Buyers near the southern and eastern edges should confirm whether a home is in Mecklenburg or Union County, and in North or South Carolina.

overview: Mint Hill is a suburban town on Charlotte's southeast edge, located mostly in Mecklenburg County with a small portion in Union County. It is near the Cabarrus County line, and its population was 26,450 at the 2020 census, up from 22,722 in 2010.

Housing is mainly single-family homes, ranging from older homes on larger lots to newer subdivisions and some townhomes, with pockets of acreage remaining in the outer areas. Mint Hill has its own town government and a small downtown area along Matthews-Mint Hill Road, and residents are close to Matthews and east Charlotte shopping. I-485 runs along the town's western side, and Albemarle Road (NC 24/27) and Lawyers Road connect toward Charlotte. Because Mint Hill is a separate municipality, property taxes include both county and town rates. Homes in the Union County portion use different county services, so buyers should confirm the county on any listing.

overview: Union County borders Mecklenburg County to the southeast and is part of the Charlotte metropolitan area. Its county seat is Monroe, and the county's population was 238,267 at the 2020 census. Towns include Indian Trail, Stallings, Weddington, Wesley Chapel, Marvin, Waxhaw, and Monroe.

US 74 (Independence Boulevard) and the Monroe Expressway (US 74 Bypass) are the main east–west routes, while Providence Road (NC 16) and NC 84 connect western Union County toward south Charlotte. Public schools are run by Union County Public Schools, which provides address-based school lookup tools. Because Union County has its own tax rates and services, buyers comparing homes on either side of the county line should check both county and town costs.

neighborhoods.name: Lake Norman
neighborhoods.tagline: Lakeside living in Cornelius, Davidson, Huntersville, Mooresville, and beyond
overview: Lake Norman is a man-made freshwater lake about 15 miles north of Charlotte, created between 1959 and 1964 during construction of Cowans Ford Dam by Duke Energy. It is the largest man-made lake located entirely within North Carolina, covering more than 50 square miles with about 520 miles of shoreline, and it borders Catawba, Iredell, Lincoln, and Mecklenburg counties.

Lake Norman is a popular area for boating, fishing, and waterfront homes. Towns around the lake include Cornelius, Davidson, Huntersville, Mooresville, and Denver. Housing ranges from waterfront estates and lake-access communities to townhomes and newer subdivisions. I-77 is the main route to Charlotte, and parks such as Jetton Park in Cornelius and Lake Norman State Park in Troutman offer public lake access. Buyers interested in waterfront homes should check whether a property has a private dock, community access, or only a water view, and should review any Duke Energy shoreline rules.

faq.a: About 15 miles north of Charlotte.

faq.q: Which towns are on Lake Norman?
faq.a: Cornelius, Davidson, Huntersville, Mooresville, and Denver, among others.

faq.q: Is Lake Norman near the light rail?
faq.a: No. I-77 is the main route between Lake Norman and Charlotte.
